title: Concept-Based Explanations to Test for False Causal Relationships Learned by Abusive Language Classifiers
measurement_description: Stereotype/bias detection, specifically evaluating whether models learn a false causal relationship between the concept 'describing a protected group with negative emotion' and the label of abuse. One of the protected groups used in the evaluation was Muslims.
findings: All three classifiers (Jigsaw, Civil Comments, TweetEval) learned that describing a protected group (which included Muslims) with negative emotion words is a strong signal for abuse. They struggled to consider the broader context, leading to an over-reliance on this concept. The TweetEval classifier showed the highest degree of this false sufficiency, resulting in the worst performance on a challenge set designed to test this phenomenon.
